arxiv-2101-05813.title: Remarks on nuclear matter: how an ω 0 \omega_{0} condensate can spike the speed of sound, and a model of Z ⁡ ( 3 ) Z(3) baryons
arxiv-2101-05813.creator: Robert D. Pisarski
arxiv-2101-05813.description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Robert D. Pisarski. I make two comments about nuclear matter. First, I consider the effects of a coupling between the O ⁡ ( 4 ) O(4) chiral field, ϕ → \vec{\phi} , and the ω μ \omega_{\mu} meson, ∼ + ω μ 2 ​ ϕ → 2 \sim+\,\omega_{\mu}^{2}\,\vec{\phi}^{\,2} ; for any net baryon density, a condensate for ω 0 \omega_{0} is unavoidably generated.

arxiv-2108-09247.title: Flow Field Tomography with Uncertainty Quantification using a Bayesian Physics-Informed Neural Network Corresponding author: S.J. Grauer (email: sgrauer@psu.edu).
arxiv-2108-09247.creator: Joseph P. Molnar and Samuel J. Grauer
arxiv-2108-09247.description: Abstract We report a new approach to flow field tomography that uses the Navier–Stokes and advection–diffusion equations to regularize reconstructions. Tomography is increasingly employed to infer 2D or 3D fluid flow and combustion structures from a series of line-of-sight (LoS) integrated measurements using a wide array of imaging modalities.

arxiv-2202-09260.title: Strichartz estimates for equations with structured Lipschitz coefficients
arxiv-2202-09260.creator: Dorothee Frey and Robert Schippa
arxiv-2202-09260.description: Abstract . Sharp Strichartz estimates are proved for Schrödinger and wave equations with Lipschitz coefficients satisfying additional structural assumptions. We use Phillips functional calculus as a substitute for Fourier inversion, which shows how dispersive properties are inherited from the constant coefficient case. Global Strichartz estimates follow provided that the derivatives of the coefficients are integrable.

arxiv-2203-03335.title: Online Matching with Convex Delay Costs Thanks: A short version appears in the proceedings of ISAAC 2018 under the title Impatient Online Matching. This full version includes all proofs and new lower bounds.
arxiv-2203-03335.creator: Xingwu Liu, Zhida Pan, Yuyi Wang, Roger Wattenhofer
arxiv-2203-03335.description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Xingwu Liu, Zhida Pan, Yuyi Wang, Roger Wattenhofer. We investigate the problem of Min-cost Perfect Matching with Delays (MPMD) in which requests are pairwise matched in an online fashion with the objective to minimize the sum of space cost and time cost. Though linear-MPMD (i.e., time cost is linear in delay) has been thoroughly studied in the literature, it does not well model impatient requests that are common in practice.

arxiv-2208-00368.title: Skeleton-Parted Graph Scattering Networks for 3D Human Motion Prediction
arxiv-2208-00368.creator: Maosen Li, Siheng Chen ✉, Zijing Zhang, Lingxi Xie, Qi Tian, Ya Zhang ✉
arxiv-2208-00368.description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Maosen Li, Siheng Chen ✉, Zijing Zhang, Lingxi Xie, Qi Tian, Ya Zhang ✉. Graph convolutional network based methods that model the body-joints’ relations, have recently shown great promise in 3D skeleton-based human motion prediction. However, these methods have two critical issues: first, deep graph convolutions filter features within only limited graph spectrums, losing sufficient information in the full band; second, using a single graph to model the whole body underestimates the diverse patterns on various body-parts.

arxiv-2209-11680.title: An Overview of Violence Detection Techniques: Current Challenges and Future Directions
arxiv-2209-11680.creator: Nadia Mumtaz †, Naveed Ejaz †, Shabana Habib, Syed Muhammad Mohsin, Prayag Tiwari, Shahab S. Band †, Neeraj Kumar †
arxiv-2209-11680.description: Abstract The Big Video Data generated in today’s smart cities has raised concerns from its purposeful usage perspective, where surveillance cameras, among many others are the most prominent resources to contribute to the huge volumes of data, making its automated analysis a difficult task in terms of computation and preciseness.

arxiv-2309-04993.title: Thermal photon measurements at PHENIX
arxiv-2309-04993.description: Abstract Photons are emitted at all stages of relativistic heavy-ion collisions and do not interact with the medium strongly. With access to the versatility of RHIC, measurements of low momentum direct photons are made possible across different system size and beam energies.

arxiv-2405-07780.title: DirMixE: Harnessing Test Agnostic Long-tail Recognition with Hierarchical Label Variations Thanks: *: corresponding authors This work was supported in part by the National Natural Science Foundation of China: 62525212 and U23B2051, in part by the Fundamental Research Funds for the Central Universiti
arxiv-2405-07780.creator: Zhiyong Yang, Qianqian Xu*, Sicong Li, Zitai Wang
arxiv-2405-07780.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Zhiyong Yang, Qianqian Xu*, Sicong Li, Zitai Wang. This paper explores test-agnostic long-tail recognition, a challenging long-tail task where the test label distributions are unknown and arbitrarily imbalanced. We argue that the variation in these distributions can be broken down hierarchically into global and local levels. The global ones reflect a broad range of diversity, while the local ones typically arise from milder changes, often focused on a particular neighbor.

arxiv-2406-06137.title: Matrix norm shrinkage estimators and priors
arxiv-2406-06137.creator: Xiao Li 1 , Takeru Matsuda 1,2 , Fumiyasu Komaki 1,2 1 Graduate School of Information Science and Technology, The University of Tokyo, 7-3-1 Hongo, Bunkyo-ku, Tokyo 113-8656, Japan 2 RIKEN Center for Brain Science, 2-1 Hirosawa, Wako, Saitama 351-0198, Japan
arxiv-2406-06137.description: Abstract We develop a class of minimax estimators for a normal mean matrix under the Frobenius loss, which generalizes the James–Stein and Efron–Morris estimators. It shrinks the Schatten norm towards zero and works well for low-rank matrices. We also propose a class of superharmonic priors based on the Schatten norm, which generalizes Stein’s prior and the singular value shrinkage prior.

arxiv-2411-05107.title: MissionGPT: Mission Planner for Mobile Robot based on Robotics Transformer Model
arxiv-2411-05107.creator: Vladimir Berman, Artem Bazhenov, Dzmitry Tsetserukou
arxiv-2411-05107.description: Abstract This paper presents a novel approach to building mission planners based on neural networks with Transformer architecture and Large Language Models (LLMs). This approach demonstrates the possibility of setting a task for a mobile robot and its successful execution without the use of perception algorithms, based only on the data coming from the camera.

arxiv-2501-17568.title: Histogram Approaches for Imbalanced Data Streams Regression
arxiv-2501-17568.creator: Ehsan Aminian, Rita P. Ribeiro, Joao Gama
arxiv-2501-17568.description: Abstract Imbalanced domains pose a significant challenge in real-world predictive analytics, particularly in the context of regression. While existing research has primarily focused on batch learning from static datasets, limited attention has been given to imbalanced regression in online learning scenarios.

arxiv-2508-02376.title: Talking Surveys: How Photorealistic Embodied Conversational Agents Shape Response Quality, Engagement, and Satisfaction
arxiv-2508-02376.creator: Matus Krajcovic, Peter Demcak, Eduard Kuric
arxiv-2508-02376.description: Abstract Abstract Embodied conversational agents (ECAs) are increasingly more realistic and capable of dynamic conversations. In online surveys, anthropomorphic agents could help address issues like careless responding and satisficing, which originate from the lack of personal engagement and perceived accountability.

arxiv-2512-14662.title: Fixed-Income Pricing and the Replication of Liabilities This paper was written while the author was a guest of the FinsureTech Hub, Department of Mathematics, ETH Zurich.
arxiv-2512-14662.creator: Damir Filipović
arxiv-2512-14662.description: Abstract This paper develops a model-free framework for static fixed-income pricing and the replication of liability cash flows. We show that the absence of static arbitrage across a universe of fixed-income instruments is equivalent to the existence of a strictly positive discount curve that reproduces all observed market prices.

pmc-10557075.title: Exploring atherosclerosis imaging with contrast-enhanced MRI using PEGylated ultrasmall iron oxide nanoparticles
pmc-10557075.creator: Ruru Zhang, Kuan Lu, Li Xiao, Xuelan Hu, Wu Cai, Linjiang Liu, Yan Liu, Weihua Li, Hui Zhou, Zhiyuan Qian, Sixia Wang, Can Chen, Jianfeng Zeng, Mingyuan Gao
pmc-10557075.description: Plaque rupture is a critical concern due to its potential for severe outcomes such as cerebral infarction and myocardial infarction, underscoring the urgency of noninvasive early diagnosis. Magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) has gained prominence in plaque imaging, leveraging its noninvasiveness, high spatial resolution, and lack of ionizing radiation.

pmc-10594269.title: Active surveillance and contact precautions for preventing MRSA healthcare-associated infections during the COVID-19 pandemic
pmc-10594269.creator: Brian McCauley, Martin Evans, Loretta Simbartl, Makoto Jones, Gary Roselle, Anthony Harris, Eli Perencevich, Michael Rubin, Stephen Kralovic, Linda Flarida, Natalie Hicks
pmc-10594269.description: Background: Statistically significant decreases in methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus (MRSA) healthcare-associated infections (HAIs) occurred in Veterans Health Administration (VA) facilities from 2007 to 2019 using active surveillance for facility admissions and contact precautions for patients colonized (CPC) or infected (CPI) with MRSA, but the value of these interventions is controversial.

pmc-11333940.title: Electrocatalytic activity of tungsten carbide hybrids with two different MOFs for water splitting: a comparative analysis
pmc-11333940.creator: Umair Sohail, Erum Pervaiz, Rafiq Khosa, Maryum Ali
pmc-11333940.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). Conventional energy resources are diminishing, and environmental pollution is constantly increasing because of the excessive use of fossil fuels to sustain the ever-increasing population and industrialization. This has raised concerns regarding a sustainable future. In the pursuit of addressing sustainability in industrial processes and energy systems, the production of green hydrogen is considered a promising and crucial solution to meet the growing energy demands. Water-splitting is one of the most effective technologies for producing clean and carbon-neutral hydrogen.

pmc-11539139.title: Artificial intelligence generates proficient Spanish obstetrics and gynecology counseling templates
pmc-11539139.creator: Rachel L. Solmonovich, Insaf Kouba, Oscar Quezada, Gianni Rodriguez-Ayala, Veronica Rojas, Kevin Bonilla, Kevin Espino, Luis A. Bracero
pmc-11539139.description: BackgroundEffective patient counseling in Obstetrics and gynecology is vital. Existing language barriers between Spanish-speaking patients and English-speaking providers may negatively impact patient understanding and adherence to medical recommendations, as language discordance between provider and patient has been associated with medication noncompliance, adverse drug events, and underuse of preventative care.

pmc-12636529.title: Patient-derived induced pluripotent stem cells with a C9orf72 expansion as a model to study frontotemporal dementia pathologies
pmc-12636529.creator: Sonia Infante-Tadeo, Diane L. Barber
pmc-12636529.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). The neurodegenerative disorder frontotemporal dementia (FTD) can be caused by a repeat expansion (GGGGCC; G4C2) in C9orf72. The function of wild-type C9orf72 and the mechanism by which the C9orf72-G4C2 expansion causes FTD, however, remain unresolved. Diverse disease models, including human brain samples and differentiated neurons from patient-derived induced pluripotent stem cells (iPSCs), identified some hallmarks associated with FTD, but these models have limitations, including biopsies capturing only a static snapshot of dynamic processes and differentiated neurons being labor-intensive, costly, and postmitotic.

pmc-13073352.title: Urinary Albumin-to-Creatinine Ratio as an Independent Predictor of 90-Day Outcomes in Patients Hospitalized for Acute Decompensated Heart Failure
pmc-13073352.creator: Claudia Andreea Palcău, Livia Florentina Păduraru, Ana Maria Alexandra Stănescu
pmc-13073352.description: Background: Albuminuria reflects systemic endothelial dysfunction and cardiorenal interaction in heart failure (HF), yet its short-term prognostic value in acute decompensated HF (ADHF) remains incompletely characterized. Methods: We conducted a prospective observational cohort study including 144 patients with complete follow-up hospitalized for ADHF.

pmc-13545040.title: PHACE syndrome: a systematic literature review and illustrative case report of a patient with severe cerebrovascular and neurodevelopmental sequelae
pmc-13545040.creator: Martina Gnazzo, Laura Caiazza, Caterina Sirocchi, Laura Beccani, Silvia Faccioli, Daniela Pandarese, Lorena Menta, Sara Gambretti, Benedetta Piccolo, Emanuela Turco, Elisa Incerti, Maria Carmela Pera
pmc-13545040.description: BackgroundPHACE syndrome is a rare neurocutaneous disorder defined by the association of large segmental infantile hemangiomas of the head and neck with malformations of the posterior fossa, cerebral and cervical arteries, heart, eyes, and ventral midline structures. Although facial hemangiomas are often the presenting feature, the cerebrovascular, neurodevelopmental, and airway manifestations are responsible for the greatest long-term morbidity.
